Apple has been researching AirPods equipped with cameras for some time, with Visual Intelligence being the core feature of this product. The product was originally rumoured to launch this year, but has ultimately been delayed to some point next year before hitting the shelves.

However, we may still get a chance to see the first AirPods with cameras this year. Here's why.

When news of AirPods with cameras first circulated, the model being talked about was codenamed B798. This model is still expected to debut in 2027, and should be the more feature-rich version.

However, there's another model called B790, which is reportedly set to launch later this year. The content comes from the Power On newsletter:

For years, Apple has been developing AirPods with cameras under the codename B798. As I previously reported, this product was originally planned for a 2026 launch, and was subsequently delayed to 2027. But Apple is also developing another version under the codename B790 (Apple is famously fond of developing multiple competing versions of the same product internally).

This isn't the first time we've heard news about the B790. Last month, developer Sam Henri Gold spotted related clues in the code of iOS 27 beta 2.

The outcome still needs time to be confirmed, but there's a good chance we'll see the first version of AirPods with cameras as early as September. The differences between the B790 and B798 versions remain unclear at this point, and it's even unknown whether both versions will actually make it to market.

Previous reports have indicated that, in order to house the camera, AirPods with cameras will have stems slightly longer than those of the AirPods Pro, and will feature an LED light next to the camera to indicate when data is being sent to the cloud.
